title: Pack index
description: The `index.json` a pack build emits: the pack's tools, guardrails, agents, flows and data blocks as data, plus where each tool handler and guardrail check lives. A runtime registers the pack's primitives from it, and a pack service loads the modules it names and resolves every call by id. Any indexer (the TypeScript `kindgi-index`, the Python `python -m kindgi.pack index`) emits this shape. Determinism: every list is sorted by `id` (code-unit order), keys are sorted at every level, the file is UTF-8 JSON indented by two spaces with a trailing newline, and integral numbers carry no fraction, so the same source indexes to the same bytes. Consumers refuse an envelope `v` they don't recognize.

v.description: Envelope version. Additive fields on an existing entry shape don't bump it.

packId.description: The pack's id (`pack.id` in the pack config).

packVersion.description: The pack's version (`pack.version` in the pack config).

artifactVersion.description: This build of the pack. A pack build pins it; a local indexer defaults to `YYYYMMDD.N` (UTC date, N counting up from the previous index of the same day).

publishedAt.description: When the index was built — ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2026-09-20T14:32:07.104Z`). A pack build pins it for reproducible output.

tools.description: Tools with handler code, sorted by `id`.

guardrails.description: Guardrails whose check is pack code, sorted by `id`.

blocks.description: The pack's data blocks (schema-version 1.5.0+), sorted by `id`: each JSON file the blocks discovery pattern matches (`blocks/**/*.json` by default), one version per block. Absent when the pack has none. A deploy publishes them with the pack's agents.

env.description: The process environment the pack's code reads (`env` in `kindgi.config`; `[tool.kindgi.env]` in `pyproject.toml`). Absent when the pack declares none. A deployment injects exactly these names. With a `required` name unset or empty, the pack service isn't ready (unless its env check is `warn`); `/readyz` and `/v1/info` name it. Not `needsSpec.env`: that is per-call context.

required.description: Names the pack service needs, set and non-empty, to be ready. Sorted.

optional.description: Names the pack reads when present. Sorted. Never also in `required`.

envName.description: A process environment variable name. `KINDGI_*` names configure Kindgi and are never a pack's.

modulePath.description: The source file the primitive was declared in, relative to the pack root: forward slashes, no leading `./` (`tools/echo/index.ts`, `tools/ledger.py`). A pack service resolves it against its module root; a build may point it at a bundle instead. Several entries may share one module (a Python module can declare several tools).

jsonSchema.description: A JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12) in wire form. Open: any JSON Schema keyword is allowed, so this node carries no `additionalProperties` restriction.

openObject.description: An object whose shape is defined by the primitive's own schema (`tool.schema.json`, `guardrail.schema.json`, `agent.schema.json`, `flow.schema.json`); the index carries it as declared.

id.description: Tool id — what a pack service resolves an `invoke` by.

description.description: What the tool does — the model reads it.

version.description: The tool's version. A caller that names a version gets `tool-version-mismatch` when it differs.

input.description: JSON Schema the input must satisfy; the pack service validates before running the handler.

output.description: JSON Schema the handler's return value must satisfy; the pack service validates it.

mutating.description: Whether the tool may change something (`tool.schema.json` `mutating`). `false` makes it read-only: it runs in a dry run, and per-tool approval gates don't ask before it by default. Absent means it may.

needsApprovalWhenUnattended.description: Whether a person must say yes to every call of the tool in a run no person started, unless that run's trigger lists the tool in its `toolsAllowedUnattended` (`tool.schema.json` `needsApprovalWhenUnattended`). Absent means `false`.

pauses.description: Whether the tool may answer `pause` (`tool.schema.json` `pauses`, schema-version 1.6.0+): the runtime then sends each call a `waitToken`, and the run waits for another system's answer. Absent means `false`.

resultIsOutsideData.description: Whether the tool's results are outside data an agent reads as data, not instructions (`tool.schema.json` `resultIsOutsideData`). Absent means `false`.

storesFiles.description: Whether the tool may store files (`tool.schema.json` `storesFiles`, schema-version 1.8.0+): the runtime then sends each call a `toolFiles`, and the pack service gives its handler `files.store`. Absent means `false`.

readsFiles.description: Whether the tool may read stored files (`tool.schema.json` `readsFiles`, schema-version 1.8.0+): the runtime then sends each call a `toolFiles`, and the pack service gives its handler `files.read`. Absent means `false`.

approval.description: How an approval of a call to the tool reads (`tool.schema.json` `approval`): a title, a summary and what the call is about, with `{field}` placeholders a call's arguments fill in. Absent, an approval reads `Approve a call to <tool id>`.

spec.description: A declarative tool's spec (`tool.schema.json` `spec`, e.g. `kind: 'http'`). A runtime runs a tool that has one itself, resolving its `secretRef`s, rather than calling the pack service.

at.description: Where in the agent's turn the guardrail runs (`guardrail.schema.json` `at`). Absent: the final answer.

sees.description: What the check sees of the conversation (`guardrail.schema.json` `sees`). Absent: the turn.

checkPoints.description: The points the pack's check runs at (its `defineCheck` `points`, or the final answer when it names none), which `at` is one of. Absent for a built-in check, whose points the runtime knows; for a pack check, absent means the final answer only.

checkId.description: The check's id — what a pack service resolves a `check-invoke` by. Absent: the guardrail's `id`.

checkBuiltIn.description: The guardrail names a built-in check (`checkId`) without shipping a check of its own: `checkModulePath` is only the file it's declared in. The CLI sets it; a runtime warns about a guardrail naming a built-in without it.

configSchema.description: JSON Schema of the check's config.

config.description: What the check is configured with (`guardrail.schema.json` `config`).

budget.description: What one check may spend (`guardrail.schema.json` `budget`): the agent loop stops a check past its `maxLatencyMs`.

judgeCapabilities.description: For an `llm-judge` guardrail: what its judge model is routed by (`guardrail.schema.json` `judgeCapabilities`). An indexer refuses an `llm-judge` guardrail without it.

agent.description: An agent as declared (`agent.schema.json`). A TypeScript pack's `defineAgent` checks it in full at build; a deploy checks only its shape, its instructions' template and its output schema.

conversationPolicy.description: As declared (`agent.schema.json` `ConversationPolicy`), except `autoCloseAfterInactiveSeconds`, which is refused: a conversation never closes by itself, only when someone closes it.

output.description: Typed output (`{ schema, name?, maxRepairs? }`), its schema already JSON Schema.

toolErrors.description: How the agent's turns retry failed tool calls (`{ maxRetries?, retryOn? }`, `agent.schema.json` `toolErrors`).

parallelToolCalls.description: Whether read-only tool calls that a step asks for one after another run at the same time, up to 8 at once (`agent.schema.json` `parallelToolCalls`). A call to a read-only tool that pauses or declares connections runs on its own, since it may wait. Default true.

block.description: A data block as `POST /v1/blocks` publishes it: a prompt or settings, at one version. A prompt's `templateFile` is read into `template` when the pack is indexed, so the index holds the whole block. The runtime validates it in full (the template parses, the values satisfy their schema) when a deploy publishes it.

id.description: Dotted lowercase id, like an agent's (`acme.reply-prompt`).

version.description: Plain `major.minor.patch`: the version a deploy publishes.

content.description: A prompt's `{ template, parameters? }`, or settings' `{ values, schema? }`.

modulePath.description: The block's file, relative to the pack root (`blocks/reply-prompt.json`).

flow.description: A flow as declared (`flow.schema.json`), plus the kernel payload version.

kernelPayloadVersion.description: Version of the flow payload inside the index, independent of the envelope `v`.
